questions.q: Why isn't the DR runbook optional paperwork, according to this lesson?
options: Because it replaces the need for the failover group entirely
Because the real mechanisms built in Lessons 11-14 aren't usable during a real incident unless they're written down for someone under pressure to follow step by step
Because it's only used for marketing purposes
Because Azure requires it for billing purposes
questions.explain: The runbook turns 'we built this' into 'anyone on the team can execute this' during an actual incident.

questions.q: What should the step-by-step failover procedure section actually contain?
options: Only a link to Microsoft's documentation
The exact Switch-AzSqlDatabaseFailoverGroup command with the real resource group and server names already filled in, not a placeholder
A generic description of what a failover group is
A list of every Azure region
questions.explain: A runbook with placeholders someone has to fill in during a real incident defeats its own purpose — the real names belong in the document.

questions.q: Why does this lesson insist the runbook be written for whoever is on call, not just for the person who built this chapter?
options: Because only the original author is ever on call
Because a runbook only its author can follow fails the moment that person is unavailable — exactly the 'whoever happened to be on call' problem named in Lesson 1
Because Azure requires multiple authors by policy
There is no real reason for this
questions.explain: Writing commands with real names filled in and trigger criteria in plain language is what makes the document usable by anyone, not just its author.

questions.q: How does Chapter 7's DR drill actually use this runbook?
options: It rewrites the runbook from scratch during the drill
It tests whether this exact runbook gets someone through a real incident successfully — finding any gaps or wrong assumptions during the drill rather than during an actual disaster
The runbook is only used after Chapter 7, never during it
It ignores the runbook entirely and tests the failover group from scratch
questions.explain: The drill validates the runbook itself, which is a much better place to discover gaps than during a genuine emergency.

questions.q: What does the 'rollback / fail-back procedure' section of the runbook cover?
options: How to initially trigger the failover
How to delete the secondary server permanently
How to return to the original primary once it's healthy again, after the emergency has passed
How to change the RPO target after an incident
questions.explain: Fail-back is a distinct procedure from the initial failover — returning operations to the original primary once it's safe to do so.
